content.value: The `search_intel_events` clickstream — record, interaction, and correction signals that teach Search from how people actually search.
Search Intelligence is the telemetry layer beside Postgres Search and, more broadly, the query-side contract that the Search MOC routes both engines behind. Every query writes to

items.value: — a query was run (terms, result count).
— a result was clicked (which rank, which document).
— a query was re-issued after an obvious typo or refinement.

content.value: Together they form a clickstream: not just what users typed, but which results earned the click and which queries got abandoned and rewritten.
Two consumers read this data. The Auto Correction Loop mines
plus low-click queries to learn fixes like

, feeding the Did You Mean suggestion. And the Search Facets analytics surface aggregate the events into the facet counts and popularity signals shown beside results. The clickstream is also where future re-ranking of the BM25F / Search Vector weights would draw its training signal, validated against the Golden Eval set.
It sits next to Synonyms in the search subsystem — synonyms are hand-authored query expansions, while Search Intelligence is the learned, behaviour-derived counterpart. Both ride the same
route under HTTP API v1, which is why API and Contracts names this the query-side wire contract for Search.
